Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe p99 degradation — Zenwell production (us-west)

Hi Aditya,

We started seeing a sudden jump in p95/p99 and a surge in 5xx errors on our Zenwell production integration in us-west starting ~08:45 PDT. Traffic profile unchanged; this is impacting checkout flows for ~12% of live users. Concrete symptoms: p50 ~120ms (normal), p95 ~980ms (x6), p99 ~6.2s (was ~700ms), and intermittent 503s for long-running chat completions.

Attached are three sample request IDs: zwn-req-4521, zwn-req-4599, zwn-req-4720. We see a couple of GPU OOM traces in our sidecar logs and inflated latency on retries. This is causing revenue loss — have already paused a few campaigns.

Can you confirm this is on Redwood's hosted runtime side and share an ETA for mitigation? We need an update within 30 minutes and a mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Chu
Head of Engineering — Integrations
Zenwell Health

Subject: Re: Severe p99 degradation — Zenwell production (us-west)

Elaine — thanks for the quick flag. We're looking now. Internal owners pinned. High level plan:

1) Collect host/runtime OOM and GPU traces (attaching a support log request).
2) Immediately remove long-running prefix caching for Zenwell route and flush KV cache for the affected pool.
3) If p99 doesn't improve within 20m, shift Zenwell traffic to redwood-small-v2 (lower mem footprint) and perform rolling restarts of the affected nodes.
4) After stabilization we'll schedule a postmortem and propose a permanent fix (compaction, eviction heuristics).

Can you share the Model ID you are calling and whether you saw a sudden increase in sequence length for those request IDs? Sending Diego and Laura to ops the next steps.

I've started collecting logs; attaching a support-log-zenwell-20270403.txt stub with the meta we need.

Subject: Re: Severe p99 degradation — Zenwell production (us-west)

Quick ops update (initial triage):

- Observed repeated GPU OOMs on runtime hosts rwr-uw2-03, rwr-uw2-04 between 08:42 and 08:55 PDT. Attached gpu-oom-traces-20270403.log contains the local runtime stderr and the kernel OOM messages.
- Memory snapshots show high fragmentation on GPUs 2 and 3; free memory oscillating (small islands unusable).
- KV cache for the chat-stream route tied to Zenwell has ~1.8TB of aggregate prefix data across the pool (older policy kept everything to improve latency). Cache growth correlates with spike window.

Immediate remediation performed at 09:10 PDT:
- Forced flush of KV cache for Zenwell route (eviction policy override).
- Performed staggered rolling restart of rwr-uw2-03 -> rwr-uw2-04 -> rwr-uw2-01 (30s between restarts to avoid cold starts).
- Applied runtime flag: --force-memory-compact on restarted processes.

Result: p99 trending down; we're still monitoring. If residual errors persist, plan B is to temporarily route to model redwood-small-v2 until we complete a compaction+kernel patch.

Attaching: gpu-oom-traces-20270403.log, gpu-mem-summary-20270403.csv.

—Diego

Subject: Re: Severe p99 degradation — Zenwell production (us-west)

Elaine — quick follow-up with remediation and next steps.

What we did (completed by 09:20 PDT):
- Forced eviction of Zenwell route KV cache across the affected pool.
- Performed staggered rolling restarts of three hosts in the us-west pool with --force-memory-compact enabled.
- Monitored p99 and 5xx; p99 reduced to ~780ms by 09:35 PDT and is trending back to baseline for most traffic. A small tail remains for very long sequences; we're continuing to observe.

Short-term mitigations available right now if you want us to enable them immediately:
- Route a fraction (10-20%) of requests to redwood-small-v2 to eliminate OOM risk for long sequences.
- Pause prefix/KV caching for chat-streams until we push runtime compaction.

Next steps:
- Diego/infra will run a longer memory compaction job and prepare a patch for fragmentation handling (ETA 72 hours for staged rollout).
- We'll produce a postmortem and share proposed configuration changes (eviction thresholds, compaction cadence) by Mon 04/05 EOD. Draft attached.

Would you be available for a 30m call at 10:30 PDT to walk through what happened and agree on the mitigation (routing vs caching pause)?

Apologies for the disruption and thanks for patience — we'll prioritize Zenwell until this is fully resolved.

—Aditya
